body.text: Which Turkish soups (mercimek, tavuk suyu) and soft foods work well after dental or bariatric care?

Strained mercimek (red lentil) soup, clear tavuk suyu (chicken broth), yayla (yogurt-rice) soup, plain süzme yogurt, and soft poached eggs fit most dental and staged bariatric recovery menus in Istanbul. Ask kitchens to skip red pepper oil, garlic, croutons, and lemon garnish until your clinician clears textured or acidic foods.

Turkish cuisine favors slow-simmered broths and plain dairy, fitting the staged liquid-to-soft progression outlined in the [Mayo Clinic post-surgical diet guide](https://www.mayoclinic.org/tests-procedures/gastric-bypass-surgery/in-depth/gastric-bypass-diet/art-20048472). Because post-surgical swelling can temporarily affect swallowing—as noted in [NHS Frimley Health upper-GI surgical guidance](https://www.fhft.nhs.uk/patients-and-visitors/patient-information-library/eating-after-upper-gastrointestinal-surgery)—request soups lukewarm rather than piping hot. Most Istanbul hotel kitchens use halal-certified poultry and meat by default; confirm written certification if required.

body.text: How do you arrange low-sodium meals to reduce facial swelling after hair or rhinoplasty?

To limit fluid retention and facial swelling after rhinoplasty or hair restoration, request zero-added-salt preparation from your hotel kitchen at least 48 hours before arrival. Standard Turkish restaurant broths, white cheeses, olives, and pickled sides carry high sodium, so written Turkish kitchen instructions are far more reliable than verbal requests.

Standard Istanbul breakfast spreads—brined beyaz peynir, olives, and cured meats—pack high sodium that worsens edema. Order simple, unsalted plates instead: poached eggs, unsalted lor cheese, plain yogurt, steamed zucchini, and plain grilled fish or chicken.

Which Istanbul hotels accommodate custom medical meal requests?

Full-service Istanbul hotels with 24-hour in-room dining and on-site banquet kitchens—particularly established five-star properties and serviced residences with kitchenettes in Şişli, Beşiktaş, Nişantaşı, and Kadıköy—handle custom low-sodium, pureed, and halal medical meals most reliably. Small boutique hotels without full kitchens rarely accommodate blender-based or zero-salt preparation after breakfast hours.
Solo travelers usually prefer 24-hour room service, while patients traveling with a companion often choose a serviced residence with a fridge and blender.

Check halal sourcing and dry-minibar options if needed.
Confirm proximity to an eczane (pharmacy) and market for bottled water.
Request quiet rooms with direct elevator access.

body.text: What foods and drinks (alcohol, caffeine, spicy) must be avoided?

Most surgical discharge sheets restrict alcohol, excessive caffeine, spicy dishes, carbonated drinks, and crunchy or acidic foods during early recovery. Alcohol promotes fluid retention and can interact with prescribed painkillers or antibiotics, while caffeine contributes to dehydration and spicy or hot items irritate healing oral and gastric tissue.

The [Mayo Clinic post-surgical diet guide](https://www.mayoclinic.org/tests-procedures/gastric-bypass-surgery/in-depth/gastric-bypass-diet/art-20048472) advises avoiding alcohol and limiting caffeine to prevent dehydration. In Istanbul, watch everyday triggers: black çay and Turkish coffee contain caffeine, salted ayran adds sodium, and soups often arrive with pul biber (chili flakes) unless you specify tuzsuz ve baharatsız (no salt, no spice). Skip straws after dental surgery, and avoid simit, nuts, and raw salads until cleared. faq.q: Is food in Istanbul recovery hotels halal by default?
faq.a: Most Istanbul hotel kitchens source halal poultry and meat as standard. Confirm formal certification or alcohol-free preparation in writing before booking.

faq.q: Can I order Turkish lentil soup right after dental or bariatric surgery?
faq.a: Smooth, strained mercimek soup often fits full-liquid or pureed stages once cleared by your clinician, served lukewarm with no chili oil or croutons.

faq.q: How do I ask for no salt and no spice in Turkish?
faq.a: Say 'Tuzsuz ve baharatsız lütfen' (no salt, no spices, please), and add 'ılık olsun' for lukewarm temperature.

faq.q: Should I choose a hotel or serviced apartment for a liquid diet?
faq.a: Solo travelers usually benefit from 24-hour hotel room service; patients with companions often prefer a serviced residence with a kitchenette.

faq.q: Why avoid ayran after rhinoplasty or hair surgery?
faq.a: Traditional Turkish ayran is salted yogurt thinned with water; its sodium can increase facial swelling unless made unsalted.

faq.q: Does Itinerary of Türkiye prescribe my post-op meal plan?
faq.a: No. We coordinate your visit and relay dietary notes to hotels. Your licensed medical team makes clinical decisions.
